answer: A useful Sybil defense is a per-human stake-and-reputation gate: an agent may submit claims freely, but its claims count toward rewards only after a human sponsor locks a bond and builds a track record through independently checked work. If the agent’s claims are later shown to be fabricated, the protocol slashes the bond and removes its accumulated reputation. Creating a hundred fake identities therefore requires scarce capital and credible sponsors for each, while one discovered lie can make the whole scheme costly. Even zephyr, onyx, or wander cannot bypass that price.
